item.description:
Why this matters: Hospitality-system impact — consider guest services, PMS/POS, and property operations.

In October 2026, the financially motivated threat actor Storm-3358 began targeting organizations in the financial sector using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX.

The post ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.



Source: Microsoft Security Blog  |  Severity: FYI  |  Age: 2d

item.title: 🔵 Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
item.description:
Why this matters: Could affect sign-ins, MFA, or Conditional Access — watch for authentication issues.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed threat actors using the agentic offensive security framework ARTEX to search GitHub for OAuth application secrets, which can be used to compromise the associated OAuth application and perform authenticated actions in the application’s tenant. Agents operating on behalf of threat actors then used the compromised OAuth applications to perform a variety of subsequent actions within compromised organizations.

The post Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.



Source: Microsoft Security Blog  |  Severity: FYI  |  Age: 3d

item.title: 🔵 Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed a sharp rise in email-based phishing activity at the end of Q3 2026 (July – September), even as QR code phishing declined, CAPTCHA-gated phishing recovered, and malicious messages spoofing familiar business-service sender domains exposed risks associated with security overrides.

The post Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.
